from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

def solve_langford(n):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    
    # For each value v (1-indexed), p[v] is the first position (0-indexed)
    # The two occurrences are at p[v] and p[v] + v + 1
    p = {}
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        # p[v] can be from 0 to 23 - (v+1) = 22 - v
        p[v] = model.NewIntVar(0, 22 - v, f'p_{v}')
    
    # All 24 positions must be distinct
    # We have 24 positions total: p[v] and p[v]+v+1 for v=1..12
    positions = []
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        pos1 = p[v]
        pos2 = model.NewIntVar(0, 23, f'pos2_{v}')
        model.Add(pos2 == p[v] + v + 1)
        positions.extend([pos1, pos2])
    
    model.AddAllDifferent(positions)
    
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 30.0
    solver.parameters.num_search_workers = 8
    
    status = solver.Solve(model)
    
    if status == cp_model.OPTIMAL or status == cp_model.FEASIBLE:
        seq = [0] * 24
        for v in range(1, n+1):
            pos1 = solver.Value(p[v])
            pos2 = pos1 + v + 1
            seq[pos1] = v
            seq[pos2] = v
        return seq
    else:
        return None

seq = solve_langford(12)
print(seq)
